name: Greater Romania
summary: Greater Romania is the Romanian nationalist ideal of uniting all Romanians in one state, first realised in 1918 with Transylvania, Bessarabia and Bukovina and lost in part in 1940. Today it survives as irredentism toward Moldova and parts of Ukraine, most visibly in the Greater Romania Party. Adherents combine ethnic nationalism, Orthodox-tinged social conservatism, and a state-centred, populist approach to the economy.
scope: The interwar Greater Romania ideal (the 1918 unions and the Kingdom of Romania within its 1919-1940 borders) together with its modern irredentist expression in the Greater Romania Party under Corneliu Vadim Tudor. The core positions are territorial and national; economic, social and procedural answers are mostly inferred from the party and the wider Romanian nationalist tradition. Excludes the Iron Guard's fascist programme as a separate strand.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a defining issue, but the Greater Romania Party's social-democratic, state-interventionist economics point toward public health provision.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from the party's centre-left economic profile and statist heritage; the irredentist core says nothing on wages.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The party proposes state intervention in the economy, so a committed adherent would doubt that unregulated markets beat government.

public-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the party's state-intervention platform and national-communist nostalgia; interwar Romania also favoured state-led industrialisation.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from the party's centre-left fiscal stance and populist anti-elite rhetoric.

unions-good.rationale: Neither source documents a position; national-communist nostalgia and nationalist suspicion of class politics pull in opposite ways.

property-fundamental.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism values national property and the interwar state backed private landholding, but the modern party is statist.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from state-intervention economics and nationalist hostility to foreign-owned business.

cut-welfare.rationale: A fiscally centre-left, populist party would not endorse welfare cuts.

worker-ownership.rationale: No documented position; cooperative ownership is not part of the nationalist programme.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the party's authoritarian, law-and-order streak and ties to Ceausescu-era security culture.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Socially far-right, order-focused nationalists would reject drug legalisation; inferred, not documented.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The party's own rhetoric has drawn hate-speech accusations, and it resists restrictions seen as censorship; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: The interwar monarchy drifted into royal dictatorship and the modern party centred on a charismatic leader, Tudor, who was praised alongside Antonescu.

state-harmful.rationale: The Greater Romania ideal is a state-building project; the state is the vehicle of national unity.

limit-guns.rationale: No documented stance; order-oriented nationalists generally accept firm state control of weapons.

empower-police-military.rationale: The party campaigned for tougher law enforcement, including capital punishment, and treats the army as a guardian of the nation.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the party's socially far-right, Orthodox-nationalist moral outlook.

decide-locally.rationale: The ideal is a unitary national state; the 1923 and 1938 constitutions centralised, and nationalists reject ethnic autonomy for regions.

rehabilitation.rationale: A party built on the death penalty and tough order leans to punishment; inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Described as socially far-right and tied to Orthodox nationalism, which treats the family as the nation's base.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Social conservatism and Orthodox-national identity make opposition near-universal among adherents; inferred from the party's socially far-right label.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the Orthodox-nationalist moral stance and pronatalist national-rebirth outlook; Ceausescu-era nostalgia points the same way.

more-religion-public.rationale: Romanian nationalism ties Romanianness to Orthodoxy, and the Iron Guard's strong religious nationalism is part of the lineage.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Race-conscious redress runs against an ethnic-nationalist programme; inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the socially far-right orientation.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defending and uniting the Romanian nation and its culture is the ideology's reason for existing.

gradual-change.rationale: Greater Romania was won by sudden union in 1918 and the party stresses rebirth, though adherents also favour the monarchy and church; inferred.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Ethno-nationalists favour limiting immigration, though it is not a prominent theme in the sources.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The party is softly Eurosceptic and sovereignty-minded, though it backed EU and NATO entry.

free-trade.rationale: Statist economics and nationalism favour protection over open trade; inferred.

nation-first.rationale: National interest and unity of Romanians come before global cooperation in the party's sovereignty-focused politics.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Nationalists generally oppose interventions framed on universal rights; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: The ideal concerns redrawing borders to include Romanians, and ethno-nationalism rejects open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Industrialisation was a national goal in interwar and Ceausescu-era Romania; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: No documented stance and no clear ideological pull.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The sources show no position on technological progress, and nothing in the unification ideal pulls either way.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from nationalist-statist support for energy independence and heavy industry.

revolution-justified.rationale: Adherents hold the 1918 union as legitimate nation-making but are largely order-minded; no clear stance on revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: Populist anti-elite rhetoric makes technocracy unattractive; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: The party's nostalgia for Ceausescu's regime and its state intervention pull one way, but it is not a stated doctrine.

socialized-markets.rationale: No source records a view on worker- or publicly-owned market enterprises, so this is left neutral.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not an issue the ideology addresses.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance taxation is never discussed in the sources on this ideology, and its core goals do not bear on it.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; populist welfare leanings are offset by nationalist work-ethic themes.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Interwar Romanian industrialisation was protectionist and the party favours state economic intervention.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Interwar industrial policy emphasised heavy and arms industry, and the party's platform favours state intervention.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The 1918 resolution called for radical land reform and Romania remained overwhelmingly smallholder agrarian; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Alien to a nationalist, property-recognising programme.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Statist nationalism rejects abolishing state monetary institutions; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Carol II's 1938 regime had corporatist features but it is not part of the core ideal.

one-party-rule.rationale: Carol II dissolved parties, yet the ideal itself is territorial and the party competes in elections.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Greater Romania state was the Kingdom of Romania and its unification under the crown is celebrated, though the modern party is not monarchist.

democracy-best.rationale: Interwar Greater Romania ended in royal dictatorship while the modern party contests elections; adherents are split.

right-to-secede.rationale: Nationalists demand Romanian unity and accuse Hungarian parties of plotting Transylvanian secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: Elite-nationalist and populist strands conflict; no stated view.

political-violence-never.rationale: Mainstream adherents reject violence while the Iron Guard strand embraced it; genuinely split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Fascist-era nationalism glorified war but mainstream adherents do not state this.

separate-church-state.rationale: Orthodoxy is bound up with Romanian identity and the nationalist tradition favours church-nation links.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Orthodox nationalists favour religious influence, but Romania's legal tradition is secular civil law; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: Interwar Romania's arms industry and the party's nationalism favour a strong army, though the sources do not state superiority as aim.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Wikipedia describes the ideal as uniting people defined as Romanians in one state, with the aim of a homogeneous nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nationalism puts the nation, not class, at the centre of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Outcome equality is not a theme of the unification ideal, and the sources record no stance either way.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations to colonised nations are outside the Romanian irredentist tradition, so no position is documented.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-Romanian unification rests on shared language and ethnicity, not religion or civilisation.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Nationalist ethics favour duty to nation.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Inferred from the collectivist nationalist outlook.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy does not appear in the documented positions of this ideology.

limit-population.rationale: Nationalist demographic concern favours population growth.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Nothing in the sources links the ideology to accelerating technological disruption, so it stays neutral.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not documented; inferred from traditionalist nationalism.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian, security-minded outlook.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement looks to restoring the interwar Greater Romania and the national order lost in 1940.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Principled nationalist programme rather than pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: Adherents work via elections and statecraft.

means-match-ends.rationale: Prefigurative politics is not a concern of the ideology; no source addresses the question.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Abolishing the division of labour is a Marxist-utopian idea that has no place in an industrialising nationalist programme.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Need-based distribution is not stated in any source, and nationalism is indifferent to the question.

production-for-use.rationale: No source records a view; the question belongs to socialist economics that the ideology neither embraces nor attacks.

profit-exploitation.rationale: National-communist nostalgia suggests some sympathy, but nationalism rejects Marxist class theory.

collective-farming.rationale: Interwar land reform created smallholders; Ceausescu-era collectivisation is a different strand.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist theory, rejected by nationalist adherents.

taxation-theft.rationale: A party favouring state economic intervention would not call taxation theft; this is inferred from its statism.

harm-principle.rationale: Social conservatives favour restricting conduct for morals and nation.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The ideal prioritises the national collective; and nationalists contested minority group claims.

conscription.rationale: A security-minded nationalism favours compulsory service; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Libertarian view, alien to the ideology.

state-as-business.rationale: Statist nationalism sees citizens as members of a nation.

positive-liberty.rationale: No source places adherents on positive versus negative liberty, so the answer is neutral.

media-academia-power.rationale: Populist suspicion of elites, but no stated view.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The ideal was framed in biological and racial terms in the interwar period, but modern adherents rarely state this.

organic-representation.rationale: Carol II's regime had corporatist features but this is not core.

total-state.rationale: Authoritarian, but the ideal itself does not ask the state to direct culture and life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Nationalists speak of reviving national greatness, yet decadence rhetoric is not prominent in the sources.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The core demand is annexing Moldova, Northern Bukovina and Bessarabia.

bound-labor.rationale: The 1918 resolution demanded radical land reform, the opposite.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Nationalists regard postmodern relativism as hostile; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Moral universalism is not discussed in the sources; nationalism and Orthodox tradition pull in different directions.

single-common-good.rationale: Nationalism posits one national interest over competing group interests; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Mixed, with Tudor styling himself philo-Semitic after 2003 while earlier antisemitism persisted.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The ideal is uniting Romanians abroad with the homeland; citizenship for Romanians in Moldova and beyond is a natural corollary.

revive-national-language.rationale: Romanian was never lost, though language unity is central to the movement.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Co-determination in firms is not part of nationalist platforms and no source suggests adherents care about it.

school-vouchers.rationale: Statist outlook favours public education; inferred.

economic-freedom.rationale: The party's statist, interventionist economics suggests adherents would not tie political freedom to economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Neither the interwar state nor the modern party relied on rulers' moral example in place of law, but no source speaks to it.

national-self-determination.rationale: Greater Romania rests on Romanians' self-determination at Alba Iulia and Chernivtsi in 1918.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from ethno-nationalist priority of citizens.

work-for-welfare.rationale: No source documents a workfare position, and populist welfare leanings are offset by nationalist work-ethic themes.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nationalism holds that the nation transcends class, so partnership is the natural stance.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Nationalism treats inherited cultural institutions as the substance of the nation, so adherents would refuse to sacrifice them.

dominated-front.rationale: Not documented; the party sought EU and NATO ties.

workers-nation.rationale: National-communist heritage and nationalism prefer a national framework over the Marxist International.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest prohibition has no place in Romanian nationalist or Orthodox tradition and is not in any documented programme.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Interwar Romania used ethnic discrimination, but the ideology does not demand racial segregation by law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: This Marxist account of the state conflicts with the nationalist view of the state as embodying the whole nation.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The goal of a homogeneous Romanian nation implies minorities integrate into it.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiratorial rhetoric exists but this specific claim is not documented.

proportional-representation.rationale: No source records an electoral-system preference; interwar law favoured the governing party and the modern party uses list PR.

national-mission.rationale: The ideal is about Romania's own unification, not spreading its system.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: A socially far-right movement would deny systematic male advantage; inferred from its social conservatism.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Anti-corruption populism is central to the party's rhetoric.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Interwar racial biopolitics existed but no stated stance.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The party rejected the 2006 report on communist crimes as manipulation and praised the Ceausescu regime.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The party's state-intervention platform and the interwar state-led industrial drive contradict a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Racial tropes appeared in the ideal, but no documented stance on this.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Adherents are split, from Alba Iulia egalitarian rhetoric to ethnic hierarchy.

socialism-one-country.rationale: National communism asserted socialism in one nation.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: No source speaks to settler-colonial analysis, which sits outside the Romanian nationalist frame.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A unitary nation-state favours uniform law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Orthodox nationalists dislike proselytising but no documented stance.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: The issue is irrelevant to Romanian nationalism and unaddressed, so adherents would reject a ban.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Orthodox religious instruction is part of Romanian nationalism.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: National-communist nostalgia for the Ceausescu era suggests some sympathy, but this is inferred and not stated.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Adherents invoke popular assembly consent in 1918 yet royal and party authoritarian practice varied.

population-transfer.rationale: Antonescu era saw deportations but no stated mainstream position.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: A pacifist-libertarian rule is incompatible with an ideology demanding annexation and capital punishment.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Fascist-era social Darwinism existed but not as mainstream.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The party called for outlawing UDMR as a separatist party.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican freedom theory is not discussed in any source on this ideology.

vanguard-party.rationale: Leninist vanguardism is not part of nationalist doctrine, though the party's Ceausescu nostalgia leaves it unclear.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The sources record no stance on prioritising the poor, and populist and nationalist concerns pull in different directions.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy is not documented for this ideology.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Interwar governments repressed strikes violently; order-oriented.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The nationalist case for a homogeneous state holds multiethnic composition produced conflict.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is alien to the party-based electoral politics adherents contest.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Carol II suspended civil liberties in 1938 and the party praised Antonescu and Ceausescu, regimes that used emergency powers against internal enemies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The party's state-intervention stance makes maximum prices for staple foods a natural measure; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not documented; the party relies on its own magazine.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Ethnic nationalists favour restrictive naturalisation for outsiders while descent-based citizenship remains open.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: No source documents a pay-cap position; populist anti-elite rhetoric is the only pull.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party discipline is not discussed for this ideology.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Carol II's constitution strengthened royal power.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Orthodox nationalists accept episcopal polity of the national church; inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: The ideology is nationalist rather than clerical; the church is an ally but not the ruler.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: No source records a censorship stance for adherents, though social conservatism could point to approval.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not discussed in any source on this ideology.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall mechanisms are not part of the documented programme.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The party kept NATO presence and backed EU entry.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Forced home ownership is not part of any known nationalist programme, so adherents would reject banning rentals.

people-in-arms.rationale: Nationalists support a regular national army, and nothing suggests replacing it with militia.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reuniting Romanians divided from Romania by Soviet and post-Soviet borders, especially Moldova, is the central aim.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: No source documents this view, though populist rhetoric could suggest it.

death-penalty.rationale: Restoring capital punishment was a major plank of Tudor's 2000 campaign.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Orthodox-national social conservatism would resist school sex education; inferred from the party's socially far-right label.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Orthodox nationalists may sympathise with religion in schools, but no source documents a position on evolution.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Social conservatism would favour legal restriction; inferred from the socially far-right label.

minority-language-support.rationale: 1918 resolution promised national freedom but nationalists disputed autonomy and the 1923 constitution neglected minorities.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious-minority exemptions are not discussed, and a unitary nationalist order would resist special treatment.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Social conservatism and national conformity point against valuing eccentricity; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The ideology has no documented view on developing-world debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The sources record no view linking independence to property system change.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1918 resolution invoked a universally elected constituent assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Authoritarian industrialisation in the 1930s; not stated.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: A nation-first outlook would give priority to domestic needs over global aid duties.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: No source records a nuclear stance for Romania, which kept NATO ties.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Tudor ran for president, but no stated view.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Statist, interventionist adherents would not want banks shielded from elected governments; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Adherents claim Bessarabia, Bukovina as historic Romanian land and refuse to cede.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Soviet classification debate is not addressed by sources, though adherents resent Soviet annexations.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is not documented as a concern.

collective-defense.rationale: The party kept Romania's NATO membership, which rests on mutual defence.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Soviet annexation of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina in 1940 is held unlawful.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Greater Romania was a monarchy, with the crown as national symbol, though Carol II was partisan in practice.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Romanian monarchy was honoured but never claimed divine descent, so adherents would reject this.

flat-income-tax.rationale: A fiscally centre-left party would more likely favour progressive rates; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: The ethnocentric framing of Romanian identity as biologically defined implies innate national traits.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Carol II's royal dictatorship, but not core.

space-expansion.rationale: No source links the ideology to space exploration.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-government theory is not discussed in the sources on this ideology.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court presumptions are not addressed in the sources.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Greater Romania demands uniting Romanian-populated lands in neighbouring states, the ideal summed up as from the Dniester to the Tisza.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred: a nationalist ideal that stresses national unity across classes rejects Marxist class-struggle doctrine, though the modern party is nostalgic for Ceausescu.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred: the movement defends property and tradition and the interwar land reform was done by liberal governments; the modern party takes no stand.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed; the ideal concerns uniting Romanians, and the 1940 population losses made return a concern, but no stated position exists.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred: Romanian nationalism ties nation to Orthodoxy but Romania's law and the party have not sought legal penalties for leaving religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred: nothing in Romanian nationalism points to compulsory dress for women, and Orthodox tradition has no such legal demand.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from nationalist emphasis on sovereignty; the Greater Romania Party was Eurosceptic.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The ideal is to unite all Romanians, including Moldova's, across existing borders in one state.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The 1918 Alba Iulia resolution promised minorities their own schools and administration, but the nationalist ideal is a unitary Romanian nation-state and the party opposed Hungarian autonomy.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred: the ideal wants Romanians in neighbouring states to be united with Romania, but where that is not possible it would back minority rights for them there.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Inferred: nationalism takes the nation, history and culture as drivers, not economic modes of production.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred from the party's state-interventionist, populist economics.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred from the state-centred economics, which favour supporting national firms.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred from the populist, authoritarian-drifting strands; the party attacked institutional checks, though sources are thin.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred: socially conservative nationalists do not support quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred from the state-centred, protectionist nationalist economics; no colonies are involved.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed; the party's economics are populist and sources give no position.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred: moral incentives echo the Communist period which the party recalls, but its economics are not built on them.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred: the modern party works through elections; the interwar Iron Guard strand is excluded from scope.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Interwar Greater Romania was a monarchy while the modern party is republican-leaning, so adherents split.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Romanian nationalism treats national history, language and Orthodox heritage as the core of schooling and identity.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The ideal is self-determination of Romanians against Habsburg, Hungarian and Russian rule, so rule over others for their good is inferred to be rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: Ethnic and religious nationalism holds that schools should instil national pride and loyalty, as the Greater Romania Party platform stresses.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from the party's ethnic-nation stance against minority-specific privileges, not from a stated position on racial preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from the party's state-centred populism and its rejection of central bank independence.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not addressed; the party criticises market capitalism but offers no theory of its collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Romania had no empire of its own; the ideal is union of Romanians, not influence over a former imperial realm.

delink-world-market.rationale: The party is protectionist and sceptical of the EU and free trade, but delinking from the world market is not proposed.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not addressed; the party's nationalism is cross-class and has no theory of labour aristocracy.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The party's ethnic-national, state-centred outlook is inferred to favour state regulation, including against minorities' claims, over unrestricted private freedom.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The 1918 Alba Iulia resolution promised civil and minority freedoms, but the modern party prefers duties and national interest; adherents are split.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred: the ideal treats the post-war and wartime partitions of Romanian lands as unjust impositions.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from the party platform of a republican, elected presidency.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: the nationalist ideal favours a unitary national state in which minorities do not hold a veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred: not addressed directly; nationalist populists generally accept resisting a ruler seen as betraying the nation.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Alba Iulia Resolution rested on an assembly of the nation as the source of legitimacy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred: no stated position; a mainstream adherent would agree.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: no stated position; humane use is conventional in a rural tradition.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from the Orthodox-tinged conservatism of Romanian nationalism.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred: Romanian nationalism is an activist, mobilising creed.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: not a stated theme; adherents are split.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: not a stated theme; adherents are split.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from the party populist, anti-globalist economic rhetoric.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from the ethnic-nationalist emphasis on Romanians primacy in the state.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred: the question is about communist parties and has little bearing on this creed, though national independence is prized.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from the economic nationalism of the party.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Reunifying Romanian-inhabited lands lost in 1940 and held by Moldova and Ukraine is the defining demand.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: the pre-colonial versus settler frame fits poorly, though ethnic Romanian primacy is stressed.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred: the party, under Vadim Tudor, rehabilitated Antonescu and was hostile to the anti-fascist consensus.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: the party mixed anti-communism with nostalgia for national communism; adherents are split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred: no stake in the question; adherents are split.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: the nationalist tradition honours national historical figures even when contested.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from conservative, traditional populist positions.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred: not addressed; adherents are split.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist view that Romania has its own national path.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred: not addressed; the party is respectful of the army but no guardian role is stated.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred: not addressed; adherents are split.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the traditional, Orthodox family values of Romanian nationalism.

office-by-exam.rationale: The party contests elections and favours a strong elected presidency; exams for office are not in its programme. Inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The party's economic nationalism opposes sale of national assets to foreign buyers.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from Orthodox-influenced social conservatism of Romanian nationalism.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The party backs a strong president and parliamentary party discipline, not bound delegates; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from the party's state-interventionist economics, which favours state pensions.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from the party's nationalist, state-interventionist economics; private land ownership was assumed.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The party sits in parliament and accepts its budgetary role; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: The party and Romanian nationalism treat Romanian as the sole state language and oppose autonomy for Hungarian-speaking regions.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The party's economic nationalism includes keeping land and national assets in Romanian hands.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The party opposes minority-rights preferences and judges by equal citizenship; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not addressed, and adherents have no shared view.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the party's focus on Romanian unity and its hostility to foreign interference.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Romanian nationalism rejects outside domination, including Soviet control of Eastern Europe; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Populist, state-centred nationalists such as the Greater Romania Party attack elite and foreign-linked business interests; inferred from that populism.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the party's sovereigntist, anti-foreign-influence rhetoric; no source states this policy.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Nationalists concerned with the Romanian nation's size favor boosting births over immigration; inferred from the ethnic nationalism described.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the party's ethnic nationalism and hostility to foreign ownership of Romanian land.

job-guarantee.rationale: The party's state-centred, populist economics support strong state employment measures; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology is irredentist and military-nationalist rather than engaged with democratic-peace claims.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Ethnic nationalists who value the state and order are unlikely to deny a duty to obey law; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from the strong national-sovereignty emphasis, though irredentist claims on Moldova conflict with a strict ban on intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; interwar and modern sources do not state a position on union structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Tudor and the party have promoted claims of hostile minorities, notably Hungarians and Roma, acting against Romania, as documented in the party and Tudor articles.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Orthodox-tinged social conservatism of the movement opposes abolishing legal marriage; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; the party's populism favors transparency about elites but it is not stated.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from the party's economic nationalism and protectionism favoring Romanian producers.

informal-organisation.rationale: The ideal of a unified Romanian state is pursued through formal state and party institutions, and informal anarchist-style organizing is foreign to it.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from the ethnic-nationalist and sovereigntist stance of the Greater Romania Party toward EU and international bodies.

religious-nation.rationale: Romanian nationalism is closely linked to Orthodoxy, which the sources describe as part of national identity, though the core definition remains ethnic.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The movement is built on national sovereignty and unification, so ritual submission to a leading power is inferred to be rejected.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: A unitary nation-state ideal implies revenue is pooled nationally rather than retained by regions; inferred from its centralism.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: No stated position on common ownership; state-centred populism offers no clear answer.

defeat-communism.rationale: The nationalist right is hostile to communism and Soviet influence, though Tudor praised Ceausescu; inferred with low confidence.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: State-centred economics inferred to favour direct state provision over private providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: The nationalism is tied to the Orthodox church, so adherents are inferred to deny that religion will fade.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Not addressed; the party mixes state-interventionist and nationalist economics.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Adherents are socially conservative and unlikely to link women's equality to economic transformation; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Traditional, family-centred conservatism is inferred to prefer private childcare.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Ethnic and cultural nationalism is inferred to favour defending the national language from foreign words.

treaties-binding.rationale: Alba Iulia promised minority freedoms but a nationalist unitary state would reserve the right to revise them; inferred from the party's hostility to minority parties.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The ideal is a unitary nation-state, not self-governing communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Ethnic homogeneity is a stated aim of Romanian nationalism, which makes majority settlement in minority areas a fitting tool; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The party's state-centred populism claims to avoid both liberal capitalism and communism; inferred, not a stated doctrine.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Greater Romania rests on the claim to unite all historically Romanian lands, including Moldova and Bukovina, in one state.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the party's nostalgia for Antonescu-era nationalism has led to denial claims, but its leader later disavowed them, so adherents are split.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from the Orthodox-tinged social conservatism of the movement and party, though Romania decriminalised in 2001.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The party's authoritarian drift and Ceausescu nostalgia point toward this, though it operates as a legal party; inferred.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Romanian nationalism ties national identity to Orthodoxy, so adherents lean toward this, but the sources do not state it.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Romania had no overseas colonies and the question is not addressed in the sources.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Orthodox nationalists reject this as a Muslim doctrine and their Islam stance is hostile.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Orthodox ties exist but the movement does not hold that rulers can be removed by force on religious grounds.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The movement is state-centred and populist, so it favours strong leaders over direct participation; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred from ethnic nationalism and social conservatism, which reject this framing.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the Orthodox-tinged social conservatism of Greater Romania Party adherents.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from Orthodox Church teaching, which the nationalism embraces.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The Greater Romania Party combines nationalist and left-leaning economic positions, which fits both views; the sources do not state it.

alienated-labor.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents have no view on alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Romanian nationalism ties national identity to Orthodoxy and the party has been hostile to minorities; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred from the religious nationalism that links the nation to Orthodoxy, though the 1918 resolution rests on popular self-determination.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Orthodox nationalists are split between secular state and religious presence.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and the movement has no position on employment contracts.

social-market-economy.rationale: The party's state-centred, nominally centre-left economics rejects laissez-faire but also favours state intervention beyond a social market; split.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The nationalism is built on defending and extending the national state, including by force of arms, so it cannot imagine abolishing the army.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from the party's populist, state-centred economics that favour even sharing over uneven growth.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Romanian nationalists have favoured alliances to secure the 1918 borders, although the party was sceptical of NATO and the EU; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Interwar Greater Romania was a monarchy, but the modern Greater Romania Party is republican in outlook; adherents are split.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The state-centred economic approach implies state credit and not mutual banks; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The Greater Romania Party's populism attacked foreign dictates and IMF conditions; inferred from its sovereigntist stance.

property-franchise.rationale: The 1918 Alba Iulia Resolution promised universal suffrage for all, and the party's populism is not elitist; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Adherents hold Orthodox-tinged social conservatism and have no ecofeminist outlook; inferred.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept foreign to Romanian nationalism, though party nostalgia for national communism gives mild sympathy for anti-market critique; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The party attacked media owners yet values national press; no stated position, so inferred as split.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The party demanded strong state authority but also the constitutional order; no stated position, inferred as split.

racial-franchise.rationale: Adherents hold ethnic nationalism and distrust the Hungarian minority, but the Alba Iulia Resolution promised equal rights to co-inhabiting nationalities; inferred.

online-participation.rationale: No stated position; adherents are split and the answer is inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: No stated position; the party's anti-corruption rhetoric pulls one way, secrecy and nationalism the other.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Orthodox-tinged conservatism favours same-faith marriage, but no legal restriction is a stated aim of the party; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The party was accused of antisemitic and anti-Hungarian rhetoric, but no boycott programme is documented in the sources; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The state-centred, populist party favours strong elected leadership and the nation's historic institutions rather than chance-selected panels; inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The Orthodox-tinged social conservatism of Romanian nationalism favours preserving inherited church doctrine; inferred from that tradition.

missingStatements.text: A state may claim territory outside its borders because people of its nationality live there.
missingStatements.rationale: Greater Romania demands uniting Romanian-populated lands in neighbouring states, the ideal summed up as from the Dniester to the Tisza.

missingStatements.text: A political party representing an ethnic minority should be banned if it is suspected of working to separate a region from the country.
missingStatements.rationale: The Greater Romania Party called for outlawing the ethnic Hungarian party UDMR, accusing it of plotting Transylvanian secession.

notes: Interwar and modern strands differ: the interwar kingdom was a monarchy ending in royal dictatorship, while the modern party is populist, nominally centre-left on economics and nostalgic for Ceausescu. Most economic, social and procedural answers are inferred and low confidence, so salience may be thin.
